title: Kisii soapstone carving
summary: Carvers in the Tabaka hills of western Kenya shape soft white, pink and grey soapstone into animals, bowls, boxes and chess sets, using a panga, knives and rasps, then smooth them with sandpaper and polish with wax.
howToPlay: The framed bird shows what the block must become.
Drag over cells to chip them away; switch between the fine and broad chisel.
The outline marks the figure; dark cells show where you cut too deep.
Press Check when the shape is right.
rules: Cut away only what lies outside the outline: removing a cell inside it costs as much as leaving one outside.
Undo brings back the last stroke.
Three stars need a nearly exact figure.
heritageNote: Soapstone is dug from shallow quarries near Tabaka, in Kisii County, and whole families carve, sand and polish it by hand. The stone is so soft that a knife and water are enough to shape it.
